questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I new I wanted to do my exchange in an English speaking country and I've always been in love with the landscape in Scotland. Eventually it was the landscape that won and when looking at the universities it just made sense to go there.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. They make sure to send all the information you need and they have a whole page with information concerning arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a meeting with our advisor about witch modules we could be doing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I could choose to live with a roommate or live alone, share a bathroom or have my own and being catered (receiving meals in a dining hall) or making my own food in a shared kitchen.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I could choose to be catered and receive meals in a dining hall 3 times a day (except dinner Saturday and Sunday where I had to cook in a shared kitchen with my corridor consisting of 10 students or eat out) or making all my meals in the shared kitchen

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is definitely worth it living in halls and getting the "full experience". I would also recommend being catered because a lot of the social connections I made was from meeting people there and continuing eating my meals with them in the dining hall. I would recommend, though, to choose having your own room with your own bathroom just to have the option to pull back and just be yourself, because it can be overwhelming sometimes - especially in the beginning

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was a meeting with my advisor where I had to choose my modules. I also had to register with my passport and student ID, but it was all in the same go and didn't take more than 30 minutes in total.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Meeting with advisor

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the modules I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a period of 1 week where you can change your modules. I went to one of my chosen modules the first day and didn't find it as interesting as I thought I would, so I wrote an email to the teacher on another modules I also had considered to sit in on the lecture before changing my modules to be sure. My advice is to try out different modules before finalising your choice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses was around the same as my home institution. There was less lectures and tutorials, so it was more self-study with a lot of reading.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The lectures were in a room with only around 30 students (where in Copenhagen the lectures take place in a bigger lecture room with more than double the amount of students) and they are "only" an hour long. The tutorials also differed. In one module there was group meetings before where we discussed the texts and answered questions we then had to talk about during the tutorial. In another module the tutorial took place around a big table the students and teacher were sat around.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Sex and Gender, Anthropology of the City: From Ur to Urban Hip Hop

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend them both. They are very interesting and both teachers were very good.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Depending on the sport it can get a little expensive to join

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In general, Scotland is cheaper than Denmark. Grocery shopping in Scotland is definitely cheaper and eating out is too.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of clubs and societies are offered. In the beginning there is a fair in the sports center where every society and club has a booth where you can get information, see the available options and sign op. There was definitely something for everyone both in terms of sports clubs and societies where students shared interests.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I played football in the sports club which I would recommend. They have great facilities and coaches. I was also a member of the dog walking society and hill walking society. In the beginning you want to try out everything, but you realize that there isn't time for everything, so I mostly spend my extra time on the football team and explored Scotland with my friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Definitely explore the Highlands. It is very beautiful and there is a lot of good hiking trails. I would recommend going on guided tours because it's a lot easier (unless you rent a car). Isle of Skye is also very beautiful.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. There was also a lot of international students with different cultures, so it wasn't that monotonous.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sign up for clubs and societies!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The breakfast with beans and haggis

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and friendliness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Sign up for clubs and societies that interests you, make sure to explore the Highlands,

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Every person under the age of 22 can get free access to busses in Scotland if they sign up for a YoungScot card - make sure to do that and safe a lot of money! The card also gives you access to many museums and castles for just 1 pound until you are 26 years old.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making great friends and memories and exploring great hikes and views

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from your family and friends for so long

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
